item.title: Kilmer Ranch Price Cut: Hollywood hideaway lists at $33m; finally sells for $18.5m
item.description: In 2011, Val Kilmer’s scenic Pecos River ranch in New Mexico changed hands after years on the market. Initially listed at $33 million, the asking price dropped to $18.5 million. The ranch not only boasted abundant natural beauty and guest facilities but also held a storied connection with Hollywood. Eventually, it was acquired by Texas oil tycoon Benjamin A. Strickling III and his wife, concluding Kilmer's chapter with the property.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Florida commissioners unanimously rejected development across nearly 230 acres in 2025
item.description: In a surprising turn of events, Orange County commissioners have given the green light to the Tuscana land-use plan, previously halted due to environmental issues. Set to introduce numerous apartments and hotels, this development raises alarms among locals about flooding and wildlife conservation in the vulnerable Shingle Creek Basin. Activists and residents are now rallying to influence upcoming elections, aiming to protect their community's environment.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 2003, Mies van der Rohe's Farnsworth House went to auction as buyers considered moving it away
item.description: In 2003, the Farnsworth House found itself in jeopardy as it hit the market, raising fears of dismantlement. Various prospective buyers aimed to relocate the iconic structure, jeopardizing its architectural integrity. Luckily, the National Trust for Historic Preservation and devoted locals rallied together, ultimately securing the house at auction for over $7.5 million. Today, this architectural marvel stands proudly, drawing visitors eager to experience its historical significance.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Idaho family has farmed 1,000 acres since 1950; after the state shut off its irrigation water...
item.description: An Idaho family, whose farm thrives along the Snake River, has initiated legal action against the state regarding an emergency order that ceased their irrigation due to dwindling water levels. This abrupt halt has jeopardized their crops and could threaten their agricultural enterprise. They assert that their property rights were infringed upon without due process or fair compensation, highlighting a larger issue surrounding water rights management in the region.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Avianca flight makes emergency landing in Miami after severe turbulence, at least 8 injured
item.description: An Avianca aircraft en route from Medellin, Colombia, to New York faced severe turbulence, resulting in several injuries among passengers. An emergency landing was executed in Miami early on Friday morning, where seven individuals were rushed to local hospitals—one in serious condition. The airline reaffirmed its dedication to ensuring passenger safety and provided assistance. Those unharmed resumed their journey to New York shortly thereafter.

item.title: A Florida man sold hallucinogenic cacti and mushrooms on Facebook Marketplace; 131 plants seized
item.description: A Florida man was arrested following an investigation into the alleged sale of hallucinogenic cacti and mushrooms on Facebook Marketplace. The Hillsborough County Sheriff’s Office said investigators seized 131 live plants, approximately 50 pounds of mescaline-containing cacti and 1.5 pounds of psilocybin mushrooms during a search of his home in Riverview. He faces multiple drug charges.

item.title: Pennsylvania awards $277,200 to protect 27 acres; woodland can absorb 22.5M gallons of rainwater
item.description: In a significant move for environmental conservation, a 27-acre forested area near Pittsburgh will receive lasting protection thanks to $277,200 in funding. This investment will facilitate the Lowries Run Expansion Project, essential for forest preservation. The woodland is expected to manage 22.5 million gallons of rainwater each year and eliminate more than 100,000 pounds of carbon.

item.title: Hurricane Simon intensifies rapidly as it moves across Pacific
item.description: Hurricane Simon is quickly intensifying off the Pacific coast of Mexico and is expected to reach category 4 status. A hurricane warning is currently in place from Punta San Telmo to Punta Mita. Heavy rainfall, floods, and mudslides are possible in several Mexican states due to the storm's approach. Private forecaster AccuWeather estimates that landfall may occur by early Sunday.

item.title: Global warming could enrich Russia but bring NATO closer to its doorstep
item.description: As the Arctic warms, Russia faces both opportunities and significant challenges regarding its environment and infrastructure. The Northern Sea Route is becoming a vital transit corridor, potentially boosting Russian exports to Asian markets. However, increased traffic raises risks associated with accidents and environmental harm. Despite potential economic benefits, Russia must contend with severe infrastructure damage from permafrost thaw.

item.title: Hurricane Isaias approaches US Gulf Coast, raising storm surge fears
item.description: Hurricane Isaias is gaining strength while heading towards the Gulf Coast, prompting mandatory evacuations across Florida. Energy firms are pulling personnel from offshore rigs, and significant oil and gas output is being halted. With projections of severe storm surges and heavy rain triggering potential flooding, states like Alabama and Florida have declared emergencies.
